question.name: Question 3
question.problem:
A store marked up the price of a jacket to $150%$ of its original cost. The tax on the jacket is $30%$ of its marked-up price.
If the jacket originally cost $$60,$ what is the tax on the jacket?

The tax on the jacket is $$$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, the marked-up price is $150%$ of the original cost $($60):$

$$
\begin{aligned}150%\times 60 & =\frac{150}{100}\times 60 \\  & =1.5\times 60 \\  & =90\end{aligned}
$$

So, the marked-up price of the jacket is $$90.$
Then, the tax is $30%$ of this price:

$$
\begin{aligned}30%\times 90 & =\frac{30}{100}\times 90 \\  & =0.3\times 90 \\  & =27\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tax on the jacket is $$27.$

question.problem:
A chemist increased the concentration of a lab solution to $125%$ of its original level. An additional reagent then increased that new concentration by $20%.$ If the original concentration was $80$ units, how many additional units were added solely by the reagent?

The reagent added 
{{field-1}}
additional units to the concentration.

$$
\begin{aligned}20%\times 100 & =\frac{20}{100}\times 100 \\  & =0.2\times 100 \\  & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the reagent added $20$ additional units to the concentration.

$$

links.title: The Curl of a Vector Field

questions.name: Question 1
questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F+G)$ at the point $(4,3,-1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=-3\,i+z\,j+8\sqrt{x}\,\text{k},\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=-i-j.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ -3 & z & 8\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(8\sqrt{x})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(8\sqrt{x})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(-3)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(-3)]k \\  & =(0-1)i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}-0)j+(0-0)k \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+G) & =∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j+[-i-j] \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j-i-j \\  & =-2\,i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}+1)j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(4,3,-1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F+G))(4,3,-1) & =-2\,i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{4}}+1)j \\  & =-2\,i-3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 2
questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (2F+G)$ at the point $(-1,2,0)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=xyz\,i+xy\,j+{z}^{2}\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=xy\,j-x\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F+G) & =∇\times (2F)+∇\times G \\  & =2∇\times F+∇\times G\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ xyz & xy & {z}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xyz)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz)]k \\  & =(0-0)i-(0-xy)j+(y-xz)k \\  & =xy\,j+(y-xz)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F+G) & =2∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =2[xy\,j+(y-xz)\,k]+xy\,j-x\,k \\  & =2xy\,j+2(y-xz)\,k+xy\,j-x\,k \\  & =3xy\,j+(2y-2xz-x)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(-1,2,0),$ we get

$$
(∇\times (2F+G))(-1,2,0)=-6\,j+5\,k.
$$

questions.name: Question 3
questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F-G)$ at the point $(-2,0,3)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=z{e}^{y}\,i+3\,j-x\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=2x{e}^{y}\,i-2{e}^{y}\,j.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ z{e}^{y} & 3 & -x\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(-x)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(3)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(-x)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(z{e}^{y})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(3)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(z{e}^{y})]k \\  & =(0-0)i-((-1)-{e}^{y})j+(0-z{e}^{y})k \\  & =({e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G \\  & =({e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k-[2x{e}^{y}\,i-2{e}^{y}\,j] \\  & =({e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k-2x{e}^{y}\,i+2{e}^{y}\,j \\  & =-2x{e}^{y}\,i+(3{e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(-2,0,3),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-G))(-2,0,3) & =-2(-2){e}^{0}\,i+(3{e}^{0}+1)\,j-3{e}^{0}\,k \\  & =4\,i+4\,j-3\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 4
questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F-G)$ at the point $(0,2,1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡z\,i+xy\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=-i+2z\,j-x\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡z & 0 & xy\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(0)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡z)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(0)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡z)]k \\  & =(x-0)i-(y-\frac{1}{z})j+(0-0)k \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j-[-i+2z\,j-x\,k] \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j+i-2z\,j+x\,k \\  & =(x+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y-2z)j+x\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,2,1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-G))(0,2,1) & =(0+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{1}-2-2(1))j+0\,k \\  & =i-3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 5
questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (4F+G)$ at the point $(0,1,-1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=y{e}^{x}\,i+xz\,j+(y-1)\,\text{k},\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=z\,i.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (4F+G) & =∇\times (4F)+∇\times G \\  & =4∇\times F+∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ y{e}^{x} & xz & y-1\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xz)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(y{e}^{x})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xz)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{x})]k \\  & =(1-x)\,i-(0-0)\,j+(z-{e}^{x})\,k \\  & =(1-x)\,i+(z-{e}^{x})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (4F+G) & =4(∇\times F)+∇\times G \\  & =4[(1-x)\,i+(z-{e}^{x})\,k]+z\,i \\  & =4(1-x)\,i+4(z-{e}^{x})\,k+z\,i \\  & =[4(1-x)+z]\,i+4(z-{e}^{x})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,1,-1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (4F+G))(0,1,-1) & =[4(1-0)+(-1)]\,i+4(-1-{e}^{0})\,k \\  & =[4-1]\,i+4(-1-1)\,k \\  & =3\,i-8\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 6
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨y\operatorname{ln}⁡x,0,z⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=\frac{x}{y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩,\,∇f=⟨\frac{1}{y},-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,1,3).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}} & 0 \\ y\operatorname{ln}⁡x & 0 & z\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}(z)-0(0)]i-[\frac{1}{y}(z)-0(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]j+[\frac{1}{y}(0)-(-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}})(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]k \\  & =-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}}\,i-\frac{z}{y}\,j+\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}\,k \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =\frac{x}{y}⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,-\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,3) & =⟨-\frac{1(3)}{(1)^{2}},-\frac{3}{1},0⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-3,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 7
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡z,y,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=xyz.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩,\,∇f=⟨yz,xz,xy⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,1,0).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ yz & xz & xy \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡z & y & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[(xz)(0)-(y)(xy)]i-[(yz)(0)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xy)]j+[(yz)(y)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xz)]k \\  & =-x{y}^{2}\,i+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,j+(z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z)\,k \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =xyz⟨0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xy(z\operatorname{sin}⁡z-\operatorname{cos}⁡z),z({y}^{2}-x\operatorname{cos}⁡z)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,0) & =⟨-1,-(0\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0),0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 8
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x{e}^{y},z,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=x-{e}^{y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨-1,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩,\,∇f=⟨1,-{e}^{y},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(2,0,-3).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -{e}^{y} & 0 \\ x{e}^{y} & z & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-{e}^{y}(0)-0(z)]i-[1(0)-0(x{e}^{y})]j+[1(z)-(-{e}^{y})(x{e}^{y})]k \\  & =0\,i-0\,j+(z+x{e}^{2y})\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x-{e}^{y})⟨-1,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,x{e}^{2y}-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,2x{e}^{2y}+z-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(2,0,-3) & =⟨{e}^{0}-2,0,2(2){e}^{2(0)}+(-3)-(2)^{2}{e}^{0}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 9
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨0,{e}^{3x},2y⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=2x+3.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨2,0,3{e}^{3x}⟩,\,∇f=⟨2,0,0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(0,-1,4).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {e}^{3x} & 2y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[0(2y)-0({e}^{3x})]i-[2(2y)-0(0)]j+[2({e}^{3x})-0(0)]k \\  & =0\,i-4y\,j+2{e}^{3x}\,k \\  & =⟨0,-4y,2{e}^{3x}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(2x+3)⟨2,0,3{e}^{3x}⟩+⟨0,-4y,2{e}^{3x}⟩ \\  & =⟨2(2x+3),0,(6x+9){e}^{3x}⟩+⟨0,-4y,2{e}^{3x}⟩ \\  & =⟨2(2x+3),-4y,(6x+11){e}^{3x}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(0,-1,4) & =⟨2(2(0)+3),-4(-1),(6(0)+11){e}^{3(0)}⟩ \\  & =⟨6,4,11⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 10
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\sqrt{x},0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=-z.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,1,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}⟩,\,∇f=⟨0,0,-1⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(4,1,4).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ z & \sqrt{x} & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[0(0)-(-1)(\sqrt{x})]i-[0(0)-(-1)(z)]j+[0(\sqrt{x})-0(z)]k \\  & =\sqrt{x}\,i-z\,j+0\,k \\  & =⟨\sqrt{x},-z,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(-z)⟨0,1,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}⟩+⟨\sqrt{x},-z,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-z,-\frac{z}{2\sqrt{x}}⟩+⟨\sqrt{x},-z,0⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{x},-2z,-\frac{z}{2\sqrt{x}}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(4,1,4) & =⟨\sqrt{4},-2(4),-\frac{4}{2\sqrt{4}}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-8,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties
canonical_examples.problem:
Calculate $\nabla\times(3\mathbf{F} + \mathbf{G})$ at the point $(-1,1,0)$ for the vector fields $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G,$ where

$$
\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = 3x\,\mathbf{i} + y^2z\,\mathbf{j} + 2\,\mathbf{k}, \quad (\nabla\times\mathbf{G})(x,y,z) = 3y^2\,\mathbf{i} + 4z\,\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}.
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
If $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $\nabla \times (k \mathbf F) = k \nabla \times \mathbf F$

- $\nabla \times (\mathbf F + \mathbf G) = \nabla \times \mathbf F + \nabla \times \mathbf G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (3F+G) & =∇\times (3F)+∇\times G \\  & =3∇\times F+∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $\nabla \times \mathbf{F}.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ 3x & {y}^{2}z & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(2)-\frac{∂}{∂z}({y}^{2}z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(2)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(3x)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(3x)]k \\  & =(0-{y}^{2})i-(0-0)j+(0-0)k \\  & =-{y}^{2}\,i.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (3F+G) & =3∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =3[-{y}^{2}\,i]+[3{y}^{2}\,i+4z\,j+k] \\  & =-3{y}^{2}\,i+3{y}^{2}\,i+4z\,j+k \\  & =(3{y}^{2}-3{y}^{2})\,i+4z\,j+k \\  & =4z\,j+k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(-1,1,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-G))(-1,1,0) & =4(0)\,j+k=k.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z) =  \langle 0, y-z, x-y\rangle$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z) = x+y.$ Given that

$$
\nabla\times \mathbf F = \langle 0,\,-1,\,0\rangle, 
\quad
\nabla f = \langle 1,\, 1,\, 0\rangle,
$$

calculate $\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F)$ at the point $(-1,1,3).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+   \nabla f \times \mathbf F
$$

First, we compute $\nabla f \times \mathbf F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & y-z & x-y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[1\cdot (x-y)-0\cdot (y-z)]\,i-[1\cdot (x-y)-0\cdot (0)]\,j+[1\cdot (y-z)-1\cdot (0)]\,k \\  & =(x-y)\,i+(y-x)\,j+(y-z)\,k \\  & =⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x+y)⟨0,-1,0⟩+⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-(x+y),0⟩+⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩ \\  & =⟨x-y,\,-2x,\,y-z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(-1,1,3) & =⟨(-1)-1,\,-2(-1),\,1-3⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: The Product Rule for Curl
tutorials.problem:
Recall that for functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ the product rule for differentiation is given by

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d }{\textrm d x}(f\cdot g) = f\dfrac{\textrm d }{\textrm d x}(g) +  g\dfrac{\textrm d }{\textrm d x}(f).
$$

There is an analogous rule for computing the curl of the product of a vector field and a scalar field.

Suppose that $\mathbf F$ is a vector field and $f$ is a scalar field. Then, we have the following identity:

$$
\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \, \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+   \nabla \! f \times \mathbf F
$$

where $\nabla f$ is the gradient of $f.$

Notice that the del operator $\nabla$ acts on the terms in the same way as the $\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}$ operator in the product rule for differentiation!

There are a few other tips that we can use to remember this rule:

- The term $\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F)$ on the left-hand side must be a vector field because it's a curl. So, the two terms on the right-hand side must be vector fields, too.

- The term $f \, \nabla \times \mathbf {F}$ on the right-hand side is a vector field because $f$ is a scalar field, $\nabla \times \mathbf F$ is a vector field, and the product of a scalar and a vector field is a vector field. Note that this "product" is just regular multiplication.

- The term $\nabla \! f \times \mathbf F$ on the right-hand side is a vector field because both $\nabla f$ and $\mathbf F$ are vector fields, and the *cross-product* of two vector fields is a vector field.

observed_steps.worked_solution:
If $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $\nabla \times (k \mathbf F) = k \nabla \times \mathbf F$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (3F+G) & =∇\times (3F)+∇\times G \\  & =3∇\times F+∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $\nabla \times \mathbf{F}.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ 3x & {y}^{2}z & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(2)-\frac{∂}{∂z}({y}^{2}z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(2)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(3x)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(3x)]k \\  & =(0-{y}^{2})i-(0-0)j+(0-0)k \\  & =-{y}^{2}\,i.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (3F+G) & =3∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =3[-{y}^{2}\,i]+[3{y}^{2}\,i+4z\,j+k] \\  & =-3{y}^{2}\,i+3{y}^{2}\,i+4z\,j+k \\  & =(3{y}^{2}-3{y}^{2})\,i+4z\,j+k \\  & =4z\,j+k.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-G))(-1,1,0) & =4(0)\,j+k=k.\end{aligned}

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ -3 & z & 8\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(8\sqrt{x})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(8\sqrt{x})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(-3)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(-3)]k \\  & =(0-1)i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}-0)j+(0-0)k \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j.\end{aligned}

$$

Calculate ∇×(F+G) at the point (4,3,−1) for the vector fields F and G, where F(x,y,z)=−3i+zj+8xk,(∇×G)(x,y,z)=−i−j.

a

b
−j
c
3i+4k
d
4k

Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If F and G are vector fields and k is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • ∇×(kF)=k∇×F

  • ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G

First, we need to calculate ∇×F. In doing so, we get

∇×F=|ijk∂∂x∂∂y∂∂z−3z8x|=[∂∂y(8x)−∂∂z(z)]i−[∂∂x(8x)−∂∂z(−3)]j+[∂∂x(z)−∂∂y(−3)]k=(0−1)i−(4x−0)j+(0−0)k=−i−4xj.

Applying the linearity properties, we get ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G=−i−4xj+[−i−j]=−i−4xj−i−j=−2i−(4x+1)j.

Finally, evaluating at the point (4,3,−1), we get (∇×(F+G))(4,3,−1)=−2i−(44+1)j=−2i−3j.

observed_steps.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F+G) & =∇\times (2F)+∇\times G \\  & =2∇\times F+∇\times G\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ xyz & xy & {z}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xyz)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz)]k \\  & =(0-0)i-(0-xy)j+(y-xz)k \\  & =xy\,j+(y-xz)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F+G) & =2∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =2[xy\,j+(y-xz)\,k]+xy\,j-x\,k \\  & =2xy\,j+2(y-xz)\,k+xy\,j-x\,k \\  & =3xy\,j+(2y-2xz-x)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(-1,2,0),$ we get

$$
(∇\times (2F+G))(-1,2,0)=-6\,j+5\,k.
$$

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ z{e}^{y} & 3 & -x\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(-x)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(3)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(-x)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(z{e}^{y})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(3)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(z{e}^{y})]k \\  & =(0-0)i-((-1)-{e}^{y})j+(0-z{e}^{y})k \\  & =({e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G \\  & =({e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k-[2x{e}^{y}\,i-2{e}^{y}\,j] \\  & =({e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k-2x{e}^{y}\,i+2{e}^{y}\,j \\  & =-2x{e}^{y}\,i+(3{e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(-2,0,3),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-G))(-2,0,3) & =-2(-2){e}^{0}\,i+(3{e}^{0}+1)\,j-3{e}^{0}\,k \\  & =4\,i+4\,j-3\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡z & 0 & xy\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(0)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡z)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(0)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡z)]k \\  & =(x-0)i-(y-\frac{1}{z})j+(0-0)k \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j.\end{aligned}

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j-[-i+2z\,j-x\,k] \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j+i-2z\,j+x\,k \\  & =(x+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y-2z)j+x\,k.\end{aligned}

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,2,1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-G))(0,2,1) & =(0+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{1}-2-2(1))j+0\,k \\  & =i-3\,j.\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ y{e}^{x} & xz & y-1\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xz)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(y{e}^{x})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xz)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{x})]k \\  & =(1-x)\,i-(0-0)\,j+(z-{e}^{x})\,k \\  & =(1-x)\,i+(z-{e}^{x})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (4F+G) & =4(∇\times F)+∇\times G \\  & =4[(1-x)\,i+(z-{e}^{x})\,k]+z\,i \\  & =4(1-x)\,i+4(z-{e}^{x})\,k+z\,i \\  & =[4(1-x)+z]\,i+4(z-{e}^{x})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,1,-1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (4F+G))(0,1,-1) & =[4(1-0)+(-1)]\,i+4(-1-{e}^{0})\,k \\  & =[4-1]\,i+4(-1-1)\,k \\  & =3\,i-8\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 5
question.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (4F+G)$ at the point $(0,1,-1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=y{e}^{x}\,i+xz\,j+(y-1)\,\text{k},\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=z\,i.
$$
question.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (4F+G) & =∇\times (4F)+∇\times G \\  & =4∇\times F+∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ y{e}^{x} & xz & y-1\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xz)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(y{e}^{x})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xz)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{x})]k \\  & =(1-x)\,i-(0-0)\,j+(z-{e}^{x})\,k \\  & =(1-x)\,i+(z-{e}^{x})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (4F+G) & =4(∇\times F)+∇\times G \\  & =4[(1-x)\,i+(z-{e}^{x})\,k]+z\,i \\  & =4(1-x)\,i+4(z-{e}^{x})\,k+z\,i \\  & =[4(1-x)+z]\,i+4(z-{e}^{x})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,1,-1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (4F+G))(0,1,-1) & =[4(1-0)+(-1)]\,i+4(-1-{e}^{0})\,k \\  & =[4-1]\,i+4(-1-1)\,k \\  & =3\,i-8\,k.\end{aligned}

a
3i−8k
b
4k
c
2j+5k

Correct
EXPLANATION

If F and G are vector fields and k is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • ∇×(kF)=k∇×F

  • ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G

In our case, we have ∇×(4F+G)=∇×(4F)+∇×G=4∇×F+∇×G.

First, we need to calculate ∇×F. In doing so, we get ∇×F=|ijk∂∂x∂∂y∂∂zyexxzy−1|=[∂∂y(y−1)−∂∂z(xz)]i−[∂∂x(y−1)−∂∂z(yex)]j+[∂∂x(xz)−∂∂y(yex)]k=(1−x)i−(0−0)j+(z−ex)k=(1−x)i+(z−ex)k.

Finally, evaluating at the point (0,1,−1), we get (∇×(4F+G))(0,1,−1)=[4(1−0)+(−1)]i+4(−1−e0)k=[4−1]i+4(−1−1)k=3i−8k.

tutorial.name: The Product Rule for Curl
tutorial.problem:
Recall that for functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ the product rule for differentiation is given by

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d }{\textrm d x}(f\cdot g) = f\dfrac{\textrm d }{\textrm d x}(g) +  g\dfrac{\textrm d }{\textrm d x}(f).
$$

There is an analogous rule for computing the curl of the product of a vector field and a scalar field.

Suppose that $\mathbf F$ is a vector field and $f$ is a scalar field. Then, we have the following identity:

$$
\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \, \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+   \nabla \! f \times \mathbf F
$$

where $\nabla f$ is the gradient of $f.$

Notice that the del operator $\nabla$ acts on the terms in the same way as the $\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}$ operator in the product rule for differentiation!

There are a few other tips that we can use to remember this rule:

- The term $\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F)$ on the left-hand side must be a vector field because it's a curl. So, the two terms on the right-hand side must be vector fields, too.

- The term $f \, \nabla \times \mathbf {F}$ on the right-hand side is a vector field because $f$ is a scalar field, $\nabla \times \mathbf F$ is a vector field, and the product of a scalar and a vector field is a vector field. Note that this "product" is just regular multiplication.

- The term $\nabla \! f \times \mathbf F$ on the right-hand side is a vector field because both $\nabla f$ and $\mathbf F$ are vector fields, and the *cross-product* of two vector fields is a vector field.

observed_steps.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+   \nabla f \times \mathbf F
$$

First, we compute $\nabla f \times \mathbf F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & y-z & x-y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[1\cdot (x-y)-0\cdot (y-z)]\,i-[1\cdot (x-y)-0\cdot (0)]\,j+[1\cdot (y-z)-1\cdot (0)]\,k \\  & =(x-y)\,i+(y-x)\,j+(y-z)\,k \\  & =⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x+y)⟨0,-1,0⟩+⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-(x+y),0⟩+⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩ \\  & =⟨x-y,\,-2x,\,y-z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(-1,1,3) & =⟨(-1)-1,\,-2(-1),\,1-3⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Example: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z) =  \langle 0, y-z, x-y\rangle$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z) = x+y.$ Given that

$$
\nabla\times \mathbf F = \langle 0,\,-1,\,0\rangle, 
\quad
\nabla f = \langle 1,\, 1,\, 0\rangle,
$$

calculate $\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F)$ at the point $(-1,1,3).$
question.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+   \nabla f \times \mathbf F
$$

First, we compute $\nabla f \times \mathbf F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & y-z & x-y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[1\cdot (x-y)-0\cdot (y-z)]\,i-[1\cdot (x-y)-0\cdot (0)]\,j+[1\cdot (y-z)-1\cdot (0)]\,k \\  & =(x-y)\,i+(y-x)\,j+(y-z)\,k \\  & =⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x+y)⟨0,-1,0⟩+⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-(x+y),0⟩+⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩ \\  & =⟨x-y,\,-2x,\,y-z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(-1,1,3) & =⟨(-1)-1,\,-2(-1),\,1-3⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

observed_steps.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}} & 0 \\ y\operatorname{ln}⁡x & 0 & z\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}(z)-0(0)]i-[\frac{1}{y}(z)-0(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]j+[\frac{1}{y}(0)-(-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}})(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]k \\  & =-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}}\,i-\frac{z}{y}\,j+\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}\,k \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =\frac{x}{y}⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,-\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,3) & =⟨-\frac{1(3)}{(1)^{2}},-\frac{3}{1},0⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-3,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 6
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨y\operatorname{ln}⁡x,0,z⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=\frac{x}{y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩,\,∇f=⟨\frac{1}{y},-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,1,3).$
question.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}} & 0 \\ y\operatorname{ln}⁡x & 0 & z\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}(z)-0(0)]i-[\frac{1}{y}(z)-0(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]j+[\frac{1}{y}(0)-(-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}})(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]k \\  & =-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}}\,i-\frac{z}{y}\,j+\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}\,k \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =\frac{x}{y}⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,-\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,3) & =⟨-\frac{1(3)}{(1)^{2}},-\frac{3}{1},0⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-3,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨yln⁡x,0,z⟩ and the scalar field f(x,y,z)=xy. Given that ∇×F=⟨0,0,−ln⁡x⟩,∇f=⟨1y,−xy2,0⟩, calculate ∇×(fF) at the point (1,1,3).

a
⟨3,0,−2⟩
b
⟨−3,−3,0⟩
c
⟨0,2,4⟩
d
⟨−4,−2,1⟩
e
⟨1,−1,3⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We shall use the following identity: ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F

First, we compute ∇f×F. We get ∇f×F=|ijk1y−xy20yln⁡x0z|=[−xy2(z)−0(0)]i−[1y(z)−0(yln⁡x)]j+[1y(0)−(−xy2)(yln⁡x)]k=−xzy2i−zyj+xln⁡xyk=⟨−xzy2,−zy,xln⁡xy⟩.

Therefore, we have ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F=xy⟨0,0,−ln⁡x⟩+⟨−xzy2,−zy,xln⁡xy⟩=⟨0,0,−xln⁡xy⟩+⟨−xzy2,−zy,xln⁡xy⟩=⟨−xzy2,−zy,0⟩.

Finally, ∇×(fF)(1,1,3)=⟨−1(3)(1)2,−31,0⟩=⟨−3,−3,0⟩.
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule

observed_steps.name: Question 7
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule
observed_steps.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ yz & xz & xy \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡z & y & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[(xz)(0)-(y)(xy)]i-[(yz)(0)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xy)]j+[(yz)(y)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xz)]k \\  & =-x{y}^{2}\,i+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,j+(z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z)\,k \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =xyz⟨0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xy(z\operatorname{sin}⁡z-\operatorname{cos}⁡z),z({y}^{2}-x\operatorname{cos}⁡z)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,0) & =⟨-1,-(0\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0),0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 7
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡z,y,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=xyz.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩,\,∇f=⟨yz,xz,xy⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,1,0).$
question.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ yz & xz & xy \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡z & y & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[(xz)(0)-(y)(xy)]i-[(yz)(0)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xy)]j+[(yz)(y)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xz)]k \\  & =-x{y}^{2}\,i+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,j+(z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z)\,k \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =xyz⟨0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xy(z\operatorname{sin}⁡z-\operatorname{cos}⁡z),z({y}^{2}-x\operatorname{cos}⁡z)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,0) & =⟨-1,-(0\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0),0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨cos⁡z,y,0⟩ and the scalar field f(x,y,z)=xyz. Given that ∇×F=⟨0,−sin⁡z,0⟩,∇f=⟨yz,xz,xy⟩, calculate ∇×(fF) at the point (1,1,0).

a
⟨−1,1,0⟩
b
⟨−1,2,1⟩
c
⟨0,1,2⟩
d
⟨2,−1,2⟩

⟨−2,−2,0⟩
Submit
Incorrect

We shall use the following identity: ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F

First, we compute ∇f×F. We get

∇f×F=|ijkyzxzxycos⁡zy0|=[(xz)(0)−(y)(xy)]i−[(yz)(0)−(cos⁡z)(xy)]j+[(yz)(y)−(cos⁡z)(xz)]k=−xy2i+xycos⁡zj+(zy2−xzcos⁡z)k=⟨−xy2,xycos⁡z,zy2−xzcos⁡z⟩.

Therefore, we have ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F=xyz⟨0,−sin⁡z,0⟩+⟨−xy2,xycos⁡z,zy2−xzcos⁡z⟩=⟨0,−xyzsin⁡z,0⟩+⟨−xy2,xycos⁡z,zy2−xzcos⁡z⟩=⟨−xy2,−xyzsin⁡z+xycos⁡z,zy2−xzcos⁡z⟩=⟨−xy2,−xy(zsin⁡z−cos⁡z),z(y2−xcos⁡z)⟩.

observed_steps.name: Question 8
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule
observed_steps.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -{e}^{y} & 0 \\ x{e}^{y} & z & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-{e}^{y}(0)-0(z)]i-[1(0)-0(x{e}^{y})]j+[1(z)-(-{e}^{y})(x{e}^{y})]k \\  & =0\,i-0\,j+(z+x{e}^{2y})\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x-{e}^{y})⟨-1,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,x{e}^{2y}-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,2x{e}^{2y}+z-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(2,0,-3) & =⟨{e}^{0}-2,0,2(2){e}^{2(0)}+(-3)-(2)^{2}{e}^{0}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 8
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x{e}^{y},z,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=x-{e}^{y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨-1,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩,\,∇f=⟨1,-{e}^{y},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(2,0,-3).$
question.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -{e}^{y} & 0 \\ x{e}^{y} & z & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-{e}^{y}(0)-0(z)]i-[1(0)-0(x{e}^{y})]j+[1(z)-(-{e}^{y})(x{e}^{y})]k \\  & =0\,i-0\,j+(z+x{e}^{2y})\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x-{e}^{y})⟨-1,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,x{e}^{2y}-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,2x{e}^{2y}+z-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(2,0,-3) & =⟨{e}^{0}-2,0,2(2){e}^{2(0)}+(-3)-(2)^{2}{e}^{0}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨xey,z,0⟩ and the scalar field f(x,y,z)=x−ey. Given that ∇×F=⟨−1,0,−xey⟩,∇f=⟨1,−ey,0⟩, calculate ∇×(fF) at the point (2,0,−3).

a
⟨0,0,0⟩
b
⟨−1,0,−3⟩
c
⟨3,−2,1⟩
d
⟨0,3,−2⟩
e
⟨2,0,−3⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We shall use the following identity: ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F

First, we compute ∇f×F. We get ∇f×F=|ijk1−ey0xeyz0|=[−ey(0)−0(z)]i−[1(0)−0(xey)]j+[1(z)−(−ey)(xey)]k=0i−0j+(z+xe2y)k=⟨0,0,z+xe2y⟩.

Therefore, we have ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F=(x−ey)⟨−1,0,−xey⟩+⟨0,0,z+xe2y⟩=⟨ey−x,0,xe2y−x2ey⟩+⟨0,0,z+xe2y⟩=⟨ey−x,0,2xe2y+z−x2ey⟩.

Finally, ∇×(fF)(2,0,−3)=⟨e0−2,0,2(2)e2(0)+(−3)−(2)2e0⟩=⟨−1,0,−3⟩.
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule

observed_steps.name: Question 9
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule
observed_steps.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {e}^{3x} & 2y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[0(2y)-0({e}^{3x})]i-[2(2y)-0(0)]j+[2({e}^{3x})-0(0)]k \\  & =0\,i-4y\,j+2{e}^{3x}\,k \\  & =⟨0,-4y,2{e}^{3x}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(2x+3)⟨2,0,3{e}^{3x}⟩+⟨0,-4y,2{e}^{3x}⟩ \\  & =⟨2(2x+3),0,(6x+9){e}^{3x}⟩+⟨0,-4y,2{e}^{3x}⟩ \\  & =⟨2(2x+3),-4y,(6x+11){e}^{3x}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(0,-1,4) & =⟨2(2(0)+3),-4(-1),(6(0)+11){e}^{3(0)}⟩ \\  & =⟨6,4,11⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

observed_steps.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ z & \sqrt{x} & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[0(0)-(-1)(\sqrt{x})]i-[0(0)-(-1)(z)]j+[0(\sqrt{x})-0(z)]k \\  & =\sqrt{x}\,i-z\,j+0\,k \\  & =⟨\sqrt{x},-z,0⟩.\end{aligned}

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(-z)⟨0,1,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}⟩+⟨\sqrt{x},-z,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-z,-\frac{z}{2\sqrt{x}}⟩+⟨\sqrt{x},-z,0⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{x},-2z,-\frac{z}{2\sqrt{x}}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(4,1,4) & =⟨\sqrt{4},-2(4),-\frac{4}{2\sqrt{4}}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-8,-1⟩.\end{aligned}

question.worked_solution:

$$

$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ z & \sqrt{x} & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[0(0)-(-1)(\sqrt{x})]i-[0(0)-(-1)(z)]j+[0(\sqrt{x})-0(z)]k \\  & =\sqrt{x}\,i-z\,j+0\,k \\  & =⟨\sqrt{x},-z,0⟩.\end{aligned}

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(-z)⟨0,1,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}⟩+⟨\sqrt{x},-z,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-z,-\frac{z}{2\sqrt{x}}⟩+⟨\sqrt{x},-z,0⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{x},-2z,-\frac{z}{2\sqrt{x}}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(4,1,4) & =⟨\sqrt{4},-2(4),-\frac{4}{2\sqrt{4}}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-8,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨z,x,0⟩ and the scalar field f(x,y,z)=−z. Given that ∇×F=⟨0,1,12x⟩,∇f=⟨0,0,−1⟩, calculate ∇×(fF) at the point (4,1,4).

a
⟨1,4,0⟩
b
⟨−2,4,0⟩
c
⟨−4,1,1⟩
d
⟨−4,−1,−4⟩
e
⟨2,−8,−1⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We shall use the following identity: ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F

First, we compute ∇f×F. We get

∇f×F=|ijk00−1zx0|=[0(0)−(−1)(x)]i−[0(0)−(−1)(z)]j+[0(x)−0(z)]k=xi−zj+0k=⟨x,−z,0⟩.

Therefore, we have ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F=(−z)⟨0,1,12x⟩+⟨x,−z,0⟩=⟨0,−z,−z2x⟩+⟨x,−z,0⟩=⟨x,−2z,−z2x⟩.

Finally, ∇×(fF)(4,1,4)=⟨4,−2(4),−424⟩=⟨2,−8,−1⟩.

question.name: Question 1
question.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F+G)$ at the point $(4,3,-1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=-3\,i+z\,j+8\sqrt{x}\,\text{k},\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=-i-j.
$$
question.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ -3 & z & 8\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(8\sqrt{x})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(8\sqrt{x})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(-3)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(-3)]k \\  & =(0-1)i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}-0)j+(0-0)k \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+G) & =∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j+[-i-j] \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j-i-j \\  & =-2\,i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}+1)j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(4,3,-1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F+G))(4,3,-1) & =-2\,i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{4}}+1)j \\  & =-2\,i-3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Calculate ∇×(F+G) at the point (4,3,−1) for the vector fields F and G, where F(x,y,z)=−3i+zj+8xk,(∇×G)(x,y,z)=−i−j.

a
−2i−3j
b
−j
c
3i+4k
d
4k
e
−j−k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If F and G are vector fields and k is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • ∇×(kF)=k∇×F

  • ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G

First, we need to calculate ∇×F. In doing so, we get

∇×F=|ijk∂∂x∂∂y∂∂z−3z8x|=[∂∂y(8x)−∂∂z(z)]i−[∂∂x(8x)−∂∂z(−3)]j+[∂∂x(z)−∂∂y(−3)]k=(0−1)i−(4x−0)j+(0−0)k=−i−4xj.

Applying the linearity properties, we get ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G=−i−4xj+[−i−j]=−i−4xj−i−j=−2i−(4x+1)j.

last_observation.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ -3 & z & 8\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(8\sqrt{x})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(8\sqrt{x})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(-3)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(-3)]k \\  & =(0-1)i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}-0)j+(0-0)k \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+G) & =∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j+[-i-j] \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j-i-j \\  & =-2\,i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}+1)j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(4,3,-1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F+G))(4,3,-1) & =-2\,i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{4}}+1)j \\  & =-2\,i-3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate ∇×(F+G) at the point (4,3,−1) for the vector fields F and G, where F(x,y,z)=−3i+zj+8xk,(∇×G)(x,y,z)=−i−j.

a
−2i−3j
b
−j
c
3i+4k
d
4k

−j−k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If F and G are vector fields and k is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • ∇×(kF)=k∇×F

  • ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G

First, we need to calculate ∇×F. In doing so, we get

∇×F=|ijk∂∂x∂∂y∂∂z−3z8x|=[∂∂y(8x)−∂∂z(z)]i−[∂∂x(8x)−∂∂z(−3)]j+[∂∂x(z)−∂∂y(−3)]k=(0−1)i−(4x−0)j+(0−0)k=−i−4xj.

Applying the linearity properties, we get ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G=−i−4xj+[−i−j]=−i−4xj−i−j=−2i−(4x+1)j.

Finally, evaluating at the point (4,3,−1), we get (∇×(F+G))(4,3,−1)=−2i−(44+1)j=−2i−3j.

Question 1
?

Calculate ∇×(F+G) at the point (4,3,−1) for the vector fields F and G, where F(x,y,z)=−3i+zj+8xk,(∇×G)(x,y,z)=−i−j.

a
−2i−3j
b
−j
c
3i+4k
d
4k
e
−j−k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If F and G are vector fields and k is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • ∇×(kF)=k∇×F

  • ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G

First, we need to calculate ∇×F. In doing so, we get

∇×F=|ijk∂∂x∂∂y∂∂z−3z8x|=[∂∂y(8x)−∂∂z(z)]i−[∂∂x(8x)−∂∂z(−3)]j+[∂∂x(z)−∂∂y(−3)]k=(0−1)i−(4x−0)j+(0−0)k=−i−4xj.

Applying the linearity properties, we get ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G=−i−4xj+[−i−j]=−i−4xj−i−j=−2i−(4x+1)j.

Finally, evaluating at the point (4,3,−1), we get (∇×(F+G))(4,3,−1)=−2i−(44+1)j=−2i−3j.

question.name: Question 2
question.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (2F+G)$ at the point $(-1,2,0)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=xyz\,i+xy\,j+{z}^{2}\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=xy\,j-x\,k.
$$
question.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F+G) & =∇\times (2F)+∇\times G \\  & =2∇\times F+∇\times G\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ xyz & xy & {z}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xyz)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz)]k \\  & =(0-0)i-(0-xy)j+(y-xz)k \\  & =xy\,j+(y-xz)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F+G) & =2∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =2[xy\,j+(y-xz)\,k]+xy\,j-x\,k \\  & =2xy\,j+2(y-xz)\,k+xy\,j-x\,k \\  & =3xy\,j+(2y-2xz-x)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(-1,2,0),$ we get

$$
(∇\times (2F+G))(-1,2,0)=-6\,j+5\,k.
$$

Question 2
?

Calculate ∇×(2F+G) at the point (−1,2,0) for the vector fields F and G, where

F(x,y,z)=xyzi+xyj+z2k,(∇×G)(x,y,z)=xyj−xk.

a
−6j+5k
b
 −i+3k
c
 6j+2k
d
 −6i+5j
e
 3i−2j
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

If F and G are vector fields and k is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • ∇×(kF)=k∇×F

  • ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G

In our case, we have ∇×(2F+G)=∇×(2F)+∇×G=2∇×F+∇×G

First, we need to calculate ∇×F. In doing so, we get

∇×F=|ijk∂∂x∂∂y∂∂zxyzxyz2|=[∂∂y(z2)−∂∂z(xy)]i−[∂∂x(z2)−∂∂z(xyz)]j+[∂∂x(xy)−∂∂y(xyz)]k=(0−0)i−(0−xy)j+(y−xz)k=xyj+(y−xz)k.

Applying the linearity properties, we get

∇×(2F+G)=2∇×F+∇×G=2[xyj+(y−xz)k]+xyj−xk=2xyj+2(y−xz)k+xyj−xk=3xyj+(2y−2xz−x)k.

Finally, evaluating at the point (−1,2,0), we get

(∇×(2F+G))(−1,2,0)=−6j+5k.

last_observation.name: Question 2
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties
last_observation.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F+G) & =∇\times (2F)+∇\times G \\  & =2∇\times F+∇\times G\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ xyz & xy & {z}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xyz)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz)]k \\  & =(0-0)i-(0-xy)j+(y-xz)k \\  & =xy\,j+(y-xz)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F+G) & =2∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =2[xy\,j+(y-xz)\,k]+xy\,j-x\,k \\  & =2xy\,j+2(y-xz)\,k+xy\,j-x\,k \\  & =3xy\,j+(2y-2xz-x)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(-1,2,0),$ we get

$$
(∇\times (2F+G))(-1,2,0)=-6\,j+5\,k.
$$

Question 2
?

Calculate ∇×(2F+G) at the point (−1,2,0) for the vector fields F and G, where

F(x,y,z)=xyzi+xyj+z2k,(∇×G)(x,y,z)=xyj−xk.

a
−6j+5k
b
 −i+3k
c
 6j+2k
d
 −6i+5j
e
 3i−2j
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

If F and G are vector fields and k is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • ∇×(kF)=k∇×F

  • ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G

In our case, we have ∇×(2F+G)=∇×(2F)+∇×G=2∇×F+∇×G

First, we need to calculate ∇×F. In doing so, we get

∇×F=|ijk∂∂x∂∂y∂∂zxyzxyz2|=[∂∂y(z2)−∂∂z(xy)]i−[∂∂x(z2)−∂∂z(xyz)]j+[∂∂x(xy)−∂∂y(xyz)]k=(0−0)i−(0−xy)j+(y−xz)k=xyj+(y−xz)k.

Applying the linearity properties, we get

∇×(2F+G)=2∇×F+∇×G=2[xyj+(y−xz)k]+xyj−xk=2xyj+2(y−xz)k+xyj−xk=3xyj+(2y−2xz−x)k.

Finally, evaluating at the point (−1,2,0), we get

(∇×(2F+G))(−1,2,0)=−6j+5k.

Question 2
?

Calculate ∇×(2F+G) at the point (−1,2,0) for the vector fields F and G, where

F(x,y,z)=xyzi+xyj+z2k,(∇×G)(x,y,z)=xyj−xk.

a
−6j+5k
b
 −i+3k
c
 6j+2k
d
 −6i+5j
e
 3i−2j
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

If F and G are vector fields and k is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • ∇×(kF)=k∇×F

  • ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G

In our case, we have ∇×(2F+G)=∇×(2F)+∇×G=2∇×F+∇×G

First, we need to calculate ∇×F. In doing so, we get

∇×F=|ijk∂∂x∂∂y∂∂zxyzxyz2|=[∂∂y(z2)−∂∂z(xy)]i−[∂∂x(z2)−∂∂z(xyz)]j+[∂∂x(xy)−∂∂y(xyz)]k=(0−0)i−(0−xy)j+(y−xz)k=xyj+(y−xz)k.

Applying the linearity properties, we get

∇×(2F+G)=2∇×F+∇×G=2[xyj+(y−xz)k]+xyj−xk=2xyj+2(y−xz)k+xyj−xk=3xyj+(2y−2xz−x)k.

Finally, evaluating at the point (−1,2,0), we get

(∇×(2F+G))(−1,2,0)=−6j+5k.

question.name: Question 3
question.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F-G)$ at the point $(-2,0,3)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=z{e}^{y}\,i+3\,j-x\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=2x{e}^{y}\,i-2{e}^{y}\,j.
$$
question.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ z{e}^{y} & 3 & -x\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(-x)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(3)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(-x)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(z{e}^{y})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(3)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(z{e}^{y})]k \\  & =(0-0)i-((-1)-{e}^{y})j+(0-z{e}^{y})k \\  & =({e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G \\  & =({e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k-[2x{e}^{y}\,i-2{e}^{y}\,j] \\  & =({e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k-2x{e}^{y}\,i+2{e}^{y}\,j \\  & =-2x{e}^{y}\,i+(3{e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(-2,0,3),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-G))(-2,0,3) & =-2(-2){e}^{0}\,i+(3{e}^{0}+1)\,j-3{e}^{0}\,k \\  & =4\,i+4\,j-3\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Calculate ∇×(F−G) at the point (−2,0,3) for the vector fields F and G, where F(x,y,z)=zeyi+3j−xk,(∇×G)(x,y,z)=2xeyi−2eyj.

a
−k
b
5j−2k
c
−2i−5j+k
d
4i+4j−3k
e
2i+3k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If F and G are vector fields and k is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • ∇×(kF)=k∇×F

  • ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G

In our case, we have ∇×(F−G)=∇×F−∇×G.

First, we need to calculate ∇×F. In doing so, we get

∇×F=|ijk∂∂x∂∂y∂∂zzey3−x|=[∂∂y(−x)−∂∂z(3)]i−[∂∂x(−x)−∂∂z(zey)]j+[∂∂x(3)−∂∂y(zey)]k=(0−0)i−((−1)−ey)j+(0−zey)k=(ey+1)j−zeyk.

Applying the linearity properties, we get ∇×(F−G)=∇×F−∇×G=(ey+1)j−zeyk−[2xeyi−2eyj]=(ey+1)j−zeyk−2xeyi+2eyj=−2xeyi+(3ey+1)j−zeyk.

Finally, evaluating at the point (−2,0,3), we get (∇×(F−G))(−2,0,3)=−2(−2)e0i+(3e0+1)j−3e0k=4i+4j−3k.

last_observation.name: Question 3
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties
last_observation.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ z{e}^{y} & 3 & -x\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(-x)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(3)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(-x)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(z{e}^{y})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(3)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(z{e}^{y})]k \\  & =(0-0)i-((-1)-{e}^{y})j+(0-z{e}^{y})k \\  & =({e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G \\  & =({e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k-[2x{e}^{y}\,i-2{e}^{y}\,j] \\  & =({e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k-2x{e}^{y}\,i+2{e}^{y}\,j \\  & =-2x{e}^{y}\,i+(3{e}^{y}+1)\,j-z{e}^{y}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(-2,0,3),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-G))(-2,0,3) & =-2(-2){e}^{0}\,i+(3{e}^{0}+1)\,j-3{e}^{0}\,k \\  & =4\,i+4\,j-3\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem:

$$
F(x,y,z)=z{e}^{y}\,i+3\,j-x\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=2x{e}^{y}\,i-2{e}^{y}\,j.
$$

Question 3
?

Calculate ∇×(F−G) at the point (−2,0,3) for the vector fields F and G, where F(x,y,z)=zeyi+3j−xk,(∇×G)(x,y,z)=2xeyi−2eyj.

a
−k
b
5j−2k
c
−2i−5j+k
d
4i+4j−3k
e
2i+3k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If F and G are vector fields and k is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • ∇×(kF)=k∇×F

  • ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G

In our case, we have ∇×(F−G)=∇×F−∇×G.

First, we need to calculate ∇×F. In doing so, we get

∇×F=|ijk∂∂x∂∂y∂∂zzey3−x|=[∂∂y(−x)−∂∂z(3)]i−[∂∂x(−x)−∂∂z(zey)]j+[∂∂x(3)−∂∂y(zey)]k=(0−0)i−((−1)−ey)j+(0−zey)k=(ey+1)j−zeyk.

Applying the linearity properties, we get ∇×(F−G)=∇×F−∇×G=(ey+1)j−zeyk−[2xeyi−2eyj]=(ey+1)j−zeyk−2xeyi+2eyj=−2xeyi+(3ey+1)j−zeyk.

Finally, evaluating at the point (−2,0,3), we get (∇×(F−G))(−2,0,3)=−2(−2)e0i+(3e0+1)j−3e0k=4i+4j−3k.

Calculate ∇×(F−G) at the point (−2,0,3) for the vector fields F and G, where F(x,y,z)=zeyi+3j−xk,(∇×G)(x,y,z)=2xeyi−2eyj.

a
−k
b
5j−2k
c
−2i−5j+k
d
4i+4j−3k
e
2i+3k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If F and G are vector fields and k is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • ∇×(kF)=k∇×F

  • ∇×(F+G)=∇×F+∇×G

In our case, we have ∇×(F−G)=∇×F−∇×G.

First, we need to calculate ∇×F. In doing so, we get

∇×F=|ijk∂∂x∂∂y∂∂zzey3−x|=[∂∂y(−x)−∂∂z(3)]i−[∂∂x(−x)−∂∂z(zey)]j+[∂∂x(3)−∂∂y(zey)]k=(0−0)i−((−1)−ey)j+(0−zey)k=(ey+1)j−zeyk.

Applying the linearity properties, we get ∇×(F−G)=∇×F−∇×G=(ey+1)j−zeyk−[2xeyi−2eyj]=(ey+1)j−zeyk−2xeyi+2eyj=−2xeyi+(3ey+1)j−zeyk.

Finally, evaluating at the point (−2,0,3), we get (∇×(F−G))(−2,0,3)=−2(−2)e0i+(3e0+1)j−3e0k=4i+4j−3k.

question.name: Question 4
question.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F-G)$ at the point $(0,2,1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡z\,i+xy\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=-i+2z\,j-x\,k.
$$
question.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡z & 0 & xy\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(0)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡z)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(0)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡z)]k \\  & =(x-0)i-(y-\frac{1}{z})j+(0-0)k \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j-[-i+2z\,j-x\,k] \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j+i-2z\,j+x\,k \\  & =(x+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y-2z)j+x\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,2,1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-G))(0,2,1) & =(0+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{1}-2-2(1))j+0\,k \\  & =i-3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

last_observation.name: Question 4
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties
last_observation.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡z & 0 & xy\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(0)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡z)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(0)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡z)]k \\  & =(x-0)i-(y-\frac{1}{z})j+(0-0)k \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j-[-i+2z\,j-x\,k] \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j+i-2z\,j+x\,k \\  & =(x+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y-2z)j+x\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,2,1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-G))(0,2,1) & =(0+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{1}-2-2(1))j+0\,k \\  & =i-3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

question.name: Question 5
question.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (4F+G)$ at the point $(0,1,-1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=y{e}^{x}\,i+xz\,j+(y-1)\,\text{k},\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=z\,i.
$$
question.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (4F+G) & =∇\times (4F)+∇\times G \\  & =4∇\times F+∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ y{e}^{x} & xz & y-1\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xz)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(y{e}^{x})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xz)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{x})]k \\  & =(1-x)\,i-(0-0)\,j+(z-{e}^{x})\,k \\  & =(1-x)\,i+(z-{e}^{x})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (4F+G) & =4(∇\times F)+∇\times G \\  & =4[(1-x)\,i+(z-{e}^{x})\,k]+z\,i \\  & =4(1-x)\,i+4(z-{e}^{x})\,k+z\,i \\  & =[4(1-x)+z]\,i+4(z-{e}^{x})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,1,-1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (4F+G))(0,1,-1) & =[4(1-0)+(-1)]\,i+4(-1-{e}^{0})\,k \\  & =[4-1]\,i+4(-1-1)\,k \\  & =3\,i-8\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}∇\times (4F+G) & =4(∇\times F)+∇\times G \\  & =4[(1-x)\,i+(z-{e}^{x})\,k]+z\,i \\  & =4(1-x)\,i+4(z-{e}^{x})\,k+z\,i \\  & =[4(1-x)+z]\,i+4(z-{e}^{x})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,1,-1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (4F+G))(0,1,-1) & =[4(1-0)+(-1)]\,i+4(-1-{e}^{0})\,k \\  & =[4-1]\,i+4(-1-1)\,k \\  & =3\,i-8\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.name: Question 5
feedback.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (4F+G)$ at the point $(0,1,-1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=y{e}^{x}\,i+xz\,j+(y-1)\,\text{k},\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=z\,i.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (4F+G) & =∇\times (4F)+∇\times G \\  & =4∇\times F+∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ y{e}^{x} & xz & y-1\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xz)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(y{e}^{x})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xz)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{x})]k \\  & =(1-x)\,i-(0-0)\,j+(z-{e}^{x})\,k \\  & =(1-x)\,i+(z-{e}^{x})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (4F+G) & =4(∇\times F)+∇\times G \\  & =4[(1-x)\,i+(z-{e}^{x})\,k]+z\,i \\  & =4(1-x)\,i+4(z-{e}^{x})\,k+z\,i \\  & =[4(1-x)+z]\,i+4(z-{e}^{x})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,1,-1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (4F+G))(0,1,-1) & =[4(1-0)+(-1)]\,i+4(-1-{e}^{0})\,k \\  & =[4-1]\,i+4(-1-1)\,k \\  & =3\,i-8\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 6
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨y\operatorname{ln}⁡x,0,z⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=\frac{x}{y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩,\,∇f=⟨\frac{1}{y},-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,1,3).$
question.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}} & 0 \\ y\operatorname{ln}⁡x & 0 & z\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}(z)-0(0)]i-[\frac{1}{y}(z)-0(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]j+[\frac{1}{y}(0)-(-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}})(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]k \\  & =-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}}\,i-\frac{z}{y}\,j+\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}\,k \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =\frac{x}{y}⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,-\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,3) & =⟨-\frac{1(3)}{(1)^{2}},-\frac{3}{1},0⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-3,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 6
?

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨yln⁡x,0,z⟩ and the scalar field f(x,y,z)=xy. Given that ∇×F=⟨0,0,−ln⁡x⟩,∇f=⟨1y,−xy2,0⟩, calculate ∇×(fF) at the point (1,1,3).

a
⟨3,0,−2⟩
b
⟨−3,−3,0⟩
c
⟨0,2,4⟩
d
⟨−4,−2,1⟩
e
⟨1,−1,3⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We shall use the following identity: ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F

First, we compute ∇f×F. We get ∇f×F=|ijk1y−xy20yln⁡x0z|=[−xy2(z)−0(0)]i−[1y(z)−0(yln⁡x)]j+[1y(0)−(−xy2)(yln⁡x)]k=−xzy2i−zyj+xln⁡xyk=⟨−xzy2,−zy,xln⁡xy⟩.

Therefore, we have ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F=xy⟨0,0,−ln⁡x⟩+⟨−xzy2,−zy,xln⁡xy⟩=⟨0,0,−xln⁡xy⟩+⟨−xzy2,−zy,xln⁡xy⟩=⟨−xzy2,−zy,0⟩.

Finally, ∇×(fF)(1,1,3)=⟨−1(3)(1)2,−31,0⟩=⟨−3,−3,0⟩.

last_observation.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}} & 0 \\ y\operatorname{ln}⁡x & 0 & z\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}(z)-0(0)]i-[\frac{1}{y}(z)-0(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]j+[\frac{1}{y}(0)-(-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}})(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]k \\  & =-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}}\,i-\frac{z}{y}\,j+\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}\,k \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =\frac{x}{y}⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,-\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,3) & =⟨-\frac{1(3)}{(1)^{2}},-\frac{3}{1},0⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-3,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 6
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨y\operatorname{ln}⁡x,0,z⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=\frac{x}{y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩,\,∇f=⟨\frac{1}{y},-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,1,3).$
question.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}} & 0 \\ y\operatorname{ln}⁡x & 0 & z\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}(z)-0(0)]i-[\frac{1}{y}(z)-0(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]j+[\frac{1}{y}(0)-(-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}})(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]k \\  & =-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}}\,i-\frac{z}{y}\,j+\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}\,k \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =\frac{x}{y}⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,-\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,3) & =⟨-\frac{1(3)}{(1)^{2}},-\frac{3}{1},0⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-3,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 6
?

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨yln⁡x,0,z⟩ and the scalar field f(x,y,z)=xy. Given that ∇×F=⟨0,0,−ln⁡x⟩,∇f=⟨1y,−xy2,0⟩, calculate ∇×(fF) at the point (1,1,3).

a
⟨3,0,−2⟩
b
⟨−3,−3,0⟩
c
⟨0,2,4⟩
d
⟨−4,−2,1⟩
e
⟨1,−1,3⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We shall use the following identity: ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F

First, we compute ∇f×F. We get ∇f×F=|ijk1y−xy20yln⁡x0z|=[−xy2(z)−0(0)]i−[1y(z)−0(yln⁡x)]j+[1y(0)−(−xy2)(yln⁡x)]k=−xzy2i−zyj+xln⁡xyk=⟨−xzy2,−zy,xln⁡xy⟩.

Therefore, we have ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F=xy⟨0,0,−ln⁡x⟩+⟨−xzy2,−zy,xln⁡xy⟩=⟨0,0,−xln⁡xy⟩+⟨−xzy2,−zy,xln⁡xy⟩=⟨−xzy2,−zy,0⟩.

Finally, ∇×(fF)(1,1,3)=⟨−1(3)(1)2,−31,0⟩=⟨−3,−3,0⟩.

feedback.name: Question 6
feedback.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨y\operatorname{ln}⁡x,0,z⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=\frac{x}{y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩,\,∇f=⟨\frac{1}{y},-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,1,3).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}} & 0 \\ y\operatorname{ln}⁡x & 0 & z\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}(z)-0(0)]i-[\frac{1}{y}(z)-0(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]j+[\frac{1}{y}(0)-(-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}})(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]k \\  & =-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}}\,i-\frac{z}{y}\,j+\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}\,k \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =\frac{x}{y}⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,-\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,3) & =⟨-\frac{1(3)}{(1)^{2}},-\frac{3}{1},0⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-3,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 7
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡z,y,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=xyz.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩,\,∇f=⟨yz,xz,xy⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,1,0).$
question.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ yz & xz & xy \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡z & y & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[(xz)(0)-(y)(xy)]i-[(yz)(0)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xy)]j+[(yz)(y)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xz)]k \\  & =-x{y}^{2}\,i+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,j+(z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z)\,k \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =xyz⟨0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xy(z\operatorname{sin}⁡z-\operatorname{cos}⁡z),z({y}^{2}-x\operatorname{cos}⁡z)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,0) & =⟨-1,-(0\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0),0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}

question.html:
Question 7
?

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨cos⁡z,y,0⟩ and the scalar field f(x,y,z)=xyz. Given that ∇×F=⟨0,−sin⁡z,0⟩,∇f=⟨yz,xz,xy⟩, calculate ∇×(fF) at the point (1,1,0).

a
⟨−1,1,0⟩
b
⟨−1,2,1⟩
c
⟨0,1,2⟩
d
⟨2,−1,2⟩
e
⟨−2,−2,0⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We shall use the following identity: ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F

First, we compute ∇f×F. We get

∇f×F=|ijkyzxzxycos⁡zy0|=[(xz)(0)−(y)(xy)]i−[(yz)(0)−(cos⁡z)(xy)]j+[(yz)(y)−(cos⁡z)(xz)]k=−xy2i+xycos⁡zj+(zy2−xzcos⁡z)k=⟨−xy2,xycos⁡z,zy2−xzcos⁡z⟩.

Therefore, we have ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F=xyz⟨0,−sin⁡z,0⟩+⟨−xy2,xycos⁡z,zy2−xzcos⁡z⟩=⟨0,−xyzsin⁡z,0⟩+⟨−xy2,xycos⁡z,zy2−xzcos⁡z⟩=⟨−xy2,−xyzsin⁡z+xycos⁡z,zy2−xzcos⁡z⟩=⟨−xy2,−xy(zsin⁡z−cos⁡z),z(y2−xcos⁡z)⟩.

Finally, ∇×(fF)(1,1,0)=⟨−1,−(0sin⁡0−cos⁡0),0⟩=⟨−1,1,0⟩.

last_observation.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ yz & xz & xy \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡z & y & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[(xz)(0)-(y)(xy)]i-[(yz)(0)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xy)]j+[(yz)(y)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xz)]k \\  & =-x{y}^{2}\,i+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,j+(z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z)\,k \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =xyz⟨0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xy(z\operatorname{sin}⁡z-\operatorname{cos}⁡z),z({y}^{2}-x\operatorname{cos}⁡z)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,0) & =⟨-1,-(0\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0),0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 7
?

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨cos⁡z,y,0⟩ and the scalar field f(x,y,z)=xyz. Given that ∇×F=⟨0,−sin⁡z,0⟩,∇f=⟨yz,xz,xy⟩, calculate ∇×(fF) at the point (1,1,0).

a
⟨−1,1,0⟩
b
⟨−1,2,1⟩
c
⟨0,1,2⟩
d
⟨2,−1,2⟩
e
⟨−2,−2,0⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We shall use the following identity: ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F

First, we compute ∇f×F. We get

∇f×F=|ijkyzxzxycos⁡zy0|=[(xz)(0)−(y)(xy)]i−[(yz)(0)−(cos⁡z)(xy)]j+[(yz)(y)−(cos⁡z)(xz)]k=−xy2i+xycos⁡zj+(zy2−xzcos⁡z)k=⟨−xy2,xycos⁡z,zy2−xzcos⁡z⟩.

Therefore, we have ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F=xyz⟨0,−sin⁡z,0⟩+⟨−xy2,xycos⁡z,zy2−xzcos⁡z⟩=⟨0,−xyzsin⁡z,0⟩+⟨−xy2,xycos⁡z,zy2−xzcos⁡z⟩=⟨−xy2,−xyzsin⁡z+xycos⁡z,zy2−xzcos⁡z⟩=⟨−xy2,−xy(zsin⁡z−cos⁡z),z(y2−xcos⁡z)⟩.

Finally, ∇×(fF)(1,1,0)=⟨−1,−(0sin⁡0−cos⁡0),0⟩=⟨−1,1,0⟩.

feedback.name: Question 7
feedback.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡z,y,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=xyz.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩,\,∇f=⟨yz,xz,xy⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,1,0).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ yz & xz & xy \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡z & y & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[(xz)(0)-(y)(xy)]i-[(yz)(0)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xy)]j+[(yz)(y)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xz)]k \\  & =-x{y}^{2}\,i+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,j+(z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z)\,k \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =xyz⟨0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xy(z\operatorname{sin}⁡z-\operatorname{cos}⁡z),z({y}^{2}-x\operatorname{cos}⁡z)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,0) & =⟨-1,-(0\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0),0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 8
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x{e}^{y},z,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=x-{e}^{y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨-1,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩,\,∇f=⟨1,-{e}^{y},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(2,0,-3).$
question.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -{e}^{y} & 0 \\ x{e}^{y} & z & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-{e}^{y}(0)-0(z)]i-[1(0)-0(x{e}^{y})]j+[1(z)-(-{e}^{y})(x{e}^{y})]k \\  & =0\,i-0\,j+(z+x{e}^{2y})\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x-{e}^{y})⟨-1,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,x{e}^{2y}-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,2x{e}^{2y}+z-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(2,0,-3) & =⟨{e}^{0}-2,0,2(2){e}^{2(0)}+(-3)-(2)^{2}{e}^{0}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,-3⟩.\end{aligned}

question.html:
Question 8
?

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨xey,z,0⟩ and the scalar field f(x,y,z)=x−ey. Given that ∇×F=⟨−1,0,−xey⟩,∇f=⟨1,−ey,0⟩, calculate ∇×(fF) at the point (2,0,−3).

a
⟨0,0,0⟩
b
⟨−1,0,−3⟩
c
⟨3,−2,1⟩
d
⟨0,3,−2⟩
e
⟨2,0,−3⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We shall use the following identity: ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F

First, we compute ∇f×F. We get ∇f×F=|ijk1−ey0xeyz0|=[−ey(0)−0(z)]i−[1(0)−0(xey)]j+[1(z)−(−ey)(xey)]k=0i−0j+(z+xe2y)k=⟨0,0,z+xe2y⟩.

Therefore, we have ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F=(x−ey)⟨−1,0,−xey⟩+⟨0,0,z+xe2y⟩=⟨ey−x,0,xe2y−x2ey⟩+⟨0,0,z+xe2y⟩=⟨ey−x,0,2xe2y+z−x2ey⟩.

Finally, ∇×(fF)(2,0,−3)=⟨e0−2,0,2(2)e2(0)+(−3)−(2)2e0⟩=⟨−1,0,−3⟩.

We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -{e}^{y} & 0 \\ x{e}^{y} & z & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-{e}^{y}(0)-0(z)]i-[1(0)-0(x{e}^{y})]j+[1(z)-(-{e}^{y})(x{e}^{y})]k \\  & =0\,i-0\,j+(z+x{e}^{2y})\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x-{e}^{y})⟨-1,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,x{e}^{2y}-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,2x{e}^{2y}+z-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(2,0,-3) & =⟨{e}^{0}-2,0,2(2){e}^{2(0)}+(-3)-(2)^{2}{e}^{0}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨xey,z,0⟩ and the scalar field f(x,y,z)=x−ey. Given that ∇×F=⟨−1,0,−xey⟩,∇f=⟨1,−ey,0⟩, calculate ∇×(fF) at the point (2,0,−3).

a
⟨0,0,0⟩
b
⟨−1,0,−3⟩
c
⟨3,−2,1⟩
d
⟨0,3,−2⟩
e
⟨2,0,−3⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We shall use the following identity: ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F

First, we compute ∇f×F. We get ∇f×F=|ijk1−ey0xeyz0|=[−ey(0)−0(z)]i−[1(0)−0(xey)]j+[1(z)−(−ey)(xey)]k=0i−0j+(z+xe2y)k=⟨0,0,z+xe2y⟩.

Therefore, we have ∇×(fF)=f∇×F+∇f×F=(x−ey)⟨−1,0,−xey⟩+⟨0,0,z+xe2y⟩=⟨ey−x,0,xe2y−x2ey⟩+⟨0,0,z+xe2y⟩=⟨ey−x,0,2xe2y+z−x2ey⟩.

Finally, ∇×(fF)(2,0,−3)=⟨e0−2,0,2(2)e2(0)+(−3)−(2)2e0⟩=⟨−1,0,−3⟩.

feedback.name: Question 8
feedback.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x{e}^{y},z,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=x-{e}^{y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨-1,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩,\,∇f=⟨1,-{e}^{y},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(2,0,-3).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -{e}^{y} & 0 \\ x{e}^{y} & z & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-{e}^{y}(0)-0(z)]i-[1(0)-0(x{e}^{y})]j+[1(z)-(-{e}^{y})(x{e}^{y})]k \\  & =0\,i-0\,j+(z+x{e}^{2y})\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x-{e}^{y})⟨-1,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,x{e}^{2y}-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,2x{e}^{2y}+z-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(2,0,-3) & =⟨{e}^{0}-2,0,2(2){e}^{2(0)}+(-3)-(2)^{2}{e}^{0}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 9
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨0,{e}^{3x},2y⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=2x+3.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨2,0,3{e}^{3x}⟩,\,∇f=⟨2,0,0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(0,-1,4).$
question.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {e}^{3x} & 2y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[0(2y)-0({e}^{3x})]i-[2(2y)-0(0)]j+[2({e}^{3x})-0(0)]k \\  & =0\,i-4y\,j+2{e}^{3x}\,k \\  & =⟨0,-4y,2{e}^{3x}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(2x+3)⟨2,0,3{e}^{3x}⟩+⟨0,-4y,2{e}^{3x}⟩ \\  & =⟨2(2x+3),0,(6x+9){e}^{3x}⟩+⟨0,-4y,2{e}^{3x}⟩ \\  & =⟨2(2x+3),-4y,(6x+11){e}^{3x}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(0,-1,4) & =⟨2(2(0)+3),-4(-1),(6(0)+11){e}^{3(0)}⟩ \\  & =⟨6,4,11⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
